title: Top most populous countries
prompt: Name the most populous countries in the world.

source.name: World Bank Open Data — Population, total (SP.POP.TOTL), sourced from UN DESA World Population Prospects 2024 Revision

title: Top largest countries by total area
prompt: Name the largest countries in the world by total area (land + inland water).

source.name: United Nations Statistics Division — Demographic Yearbook

note: Total area = land + inland waters. Territorial seas and EEZs excluded. This UN convention places China above the US at #3.

title: Top countries by nominal GDP
prompt: Name the countries with the largest economies by nominal GDP.

source.name: IMF World Economic Outlook Database, April 2025 edition

note: Nominal GDP in USD billions, not PPP.

title: Top countries by UNESCO World Heritage Sites
prompt: Name the countries with the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

source.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
source.asOf: July 2025, after 47th session of the World Heritage Committee

note: Ties are broken alphabetically. Rank 11 (Japan/USA) and rank 14 (Canada/Turkey) are two-way ties.

title: Top most-visited countries by international tourist arrivals
prompt: Name the countries with the most international tourist arrivals.

source.name: UN Tourism (UNWTO) — World Tourism Barometer, May 2024

note: Hong Kong and Macau are excluded — they are SARs of China, not sovereign countries. Original ranks in the UNWTO list have been shifted up to reflect this.

title: Most Nobel Prize laureates by country
prompt: Name the countries with the most Nobel Prize laureates (all categories, all-time).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of Nobel laureates by country (summarizing Nobel Foundation records)

note: Attribution follows the Nobel Committee's country association for each laureate (which may include country of birth, citizenship, or affiliated institution). Some laureates count under multiple countries. Counts include Peace Prize.

title: Most Oscar wins for Best International Feature Film
prompt: Name the countries with the most Academy Awards for Best International Feature Film (formerly Best Foreign Language Film).

source.name: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) — Best International Feature Film records

note: Includes Special/Honorary Awards for foreign-language films (e.g., prior to the competitive category's 1956 inception). Germany and West Germany, and the Soviet Union and Russia, are counted separately per Academy convention.

title: Most Eurovision Song Contest wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most Eurovision Song Contest wins.

source.name: European Broadcasting Union (EBU) — Eurovision Song Contest

note: Ireland and Sweden are tied at 7 wins. Ireland is the only country to win three times in a row (1992-1994).

title: Most Michelin three-star restaurants
prompt: Name the countries with the most Michelin three-star restaurants.

source.name: Michelin Guide — 2025 Three-Star Restaurants

note: Only counts the highest tier (three Michelin stars). France total includes Monaco per Michelin's Guide France. Michelin only publishes guides in countries/regions where it operates, so unrated countries could theoretically host high-quality restaurants.

title: Largest video game markets by revenue
prompt: Name the countries with the largest video game markets by consumer revenue.

source.name: Newzoo — Global Games Market Report

note: Includes revenue from console, PC, and mobile games (excluding hardware, tax, and B2B services).

title: Most-spoken languages by native speakers (primary country)
prompt: Name the primary country (origin / largest native-speaker country) for each of the world's most-spoken native languages.

source.name: Ethnologue (26th edition) — Languages by number of native (L1) speakers

note: Each entry pairs a top-ranked language with the country most closely identified as its origin or largest native-speaker base. Ethnologue splits Chinese and Arabic into individual varieties (Mandarin, Yue, Wu; Egyptian Arabic, etc.) rather than treating each as a single macrolanguage.

title: Most English speakers by country (native + second-language)
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total English-speaking populations (native plus second-language speakers).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of countries by English-speaking population (compiled from national census and Ethnologue data)
source.asOf: Compiled from most recent national censuses (2010s-2020s)

note: Includes both native (L1) and second-language (L2) speakers. Figures are drawn from national censuses and Ethnologue and are approximate — several sources are dated.

title: Most UNESCO World Heritage Sites
prompt: Name the countries with the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

source.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — States Parties statistics

note: Includes cultural, natural, and mixed sites. Transnational sites (shared by multiple countries) are counted for each participating state party.

title: Largest total CO2 emissions (annual)
prompt: Name the countries that emit the most CO2 from fossil fuels and industry each year.

source.name: Global Carbon Project / Our World in Data — Annual CO2 emissions

note: Fossil fuel + industry CO2 only (excludes land-use change). China alone emits roughly as much as the next three combined.

title: Highest CO2 emissions per capita
prompt: Name the countries that emit the most CO2 per person from fossil fuels and industry.

source.name: Global Carbon Project / Our World in Data — Per capita CO2 emissions

note: Small oil/gas states dominate the top ranks — that's the point of this leaderboard. Excludes tiny territories under 100k population.

title: Highest share of electricity from renewables
prompt: Name the countries where renewables make up the largest share of electricity generation.

source.name: Ember — Global Electricity Review

note: Renewables = hydro + wind + solar + bioenergy + geothermal. Several countries approach 100% thanks to hydro (Norway, Paraguay, Bhutan, Nepal, DRC, Ethiopia, Costa Rica).

title: Largest installed solar power capacity
prompt: Name the countries with the most solar photovoltaic capacity installed.

source.name: IRENA — Renewable Capacity Statistics

note: China's solar fleet is bigger than the rest of the top 10 combined. Rankings shift fast — China added another ~275 GW in 2024 alone.

title: Largest installed wind power capacity
prompt: Name the countries with the most wind power capacity installed (onshore + offshore).

source.name: IRENA — Renewable Capacity Statistics / Global Wind Energy Council

note: China and the U.S. hold roughly two-thirds of global wind capacity between them.

title: Largest nuclear power generation
prompt: Name the countries that generate the most electricity from nuclear power.

source.name: IAEA PRIS / EIA International Electricity Data

note: Ranked by annual electricity generated (TWh), not reactor count. France gets ~65% of its electricity from nuclear — the highest share of any large economy.

title: Largest forest cover (% of land area)
prompt: Name the countries where forests cover the largest share of the land area.

source.name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment / World Bank

note: Excludes microstates and territories. Suriname and Guyana are the greenest countries on Earth by this measure. French Guiana would beat both but it's an overseas department of France.

title: Worst air quality (highest annual average PM2.5)
prompt: Name the countries with the worst air pollution measured as annual average PM2.5.

source.name: IQAir — World Air Quality Report

note: WHO guideline is 5 µg/m³ — the top of this list runs 15-16x higher. South Asia dominates: Bangladesh, Pakistan, India and Nepal are all in the top 10.

title: Largest coffee producers
prompt: Name the world's largest coffee-producing countries.

source.name: International Coffee Organization (ICO) — Total production by exporting countries

note: Reported in 60kg bags (the industry standard sack). Includes both Arabica and Robusta.

title: Largest wine producers
prompt: Name the world's largest wine-producing countries by volume.

source.name: International Organisation of Vine and Wine (OIV) — State of the World Vine and Wine Sector 2023

note: Measured in millions of hectolitres (mhl). 2023 was a historically low global vintage due to weather; France briefly overtook Italy as #1.

title: Highest beer consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita beer consumption.

source.name: Kirin Beer University Report — Global Beer Consumption by Country

note: Litres per person per year. Czech Republic has led this ranking every year since 1993.

title: Largest rice producers
prompt: Name the world's largest rice-producing countries (paddy rice).

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

note: Rice, paddy (unmilled). China and India together produce roughly half of the world's rice.

title: Largest wheat producers
prompt: Name the world's largest wheat-producing countries.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

note: China and India together produce roughly one-third of world wheat. Russia is by far the largest exporter.

title: Most cattle in the country
prompt: Name the countries with the largest cattle (live animal) populations.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Live animals

note: Head of cattle (bovine, excluding buffalo). India includes both dairy cattle and religiously protected populations.

title: Largest fish catch (capture fisheries)
prompt: Name the countries with the largest wild fish catches from capture fisheries.

source.name: FAO — The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture (SOFIA) 2024

note: Marine and inland capture fisheries only — excludes aquaculture. Peru's total swings wildly year-to-year with El Niño-driven anchoveta cycles.

title: Highest meat consumption per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita meat consumption.

source.name: OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2024-2033 (via Our World in Data)

note: Kilograms of meat (beef, pork, poultry, sheep) per person per year, carcass weight equivalent. Excludes seafood.

title: Longest Coastline
prompt: Name the countries with the longest total coastline.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Coastline
source.asOf: CIA World Factbook, last major update 2023-2024

note: Canada is a massive outlier — its coastline (including the Arctic archipelago) is roughly six times longer than any other country's. Methodologies differ; the CIA WFB and the World Resources Institute produce different values because coastline length is fractal and depends on measurement resolution.

title: Highest Population Density
prompt: Name the sovereign countries with the highest population density (people per km²).

source.name: World Bank — Population density (people per sq. km of land area)

note: Microstates and city-states dominate this list. Monaco (~19,000/km²) and Singapore (~8,000/km²) are near-total urban jurisdictions. Excludes dependent territories like Macau. Bangladesh is the densest country with a population above 100 million.

title: Highest Urbanization Rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest percentage of population living in urban areas.

source.name: UN DESA — World Urbanization Prospects

note: City-states (Singapore, Monaco, Vatican, Hong Kong) are 100% urban by definition. Kuwait's near-100% urban rate reflects the country being effectively a single metropolitan area (Kuwait City) surrounded by desert.

title: Highest Median Age
prompt: Name the countries with the highest median age of population.

source.name: UN World Population Prospects 2024

note: Monaco tops the list but is often excluded from UN WPP main rankings due to its small size. Japan is the most-cited leader among major economies. Median age is the age that divides the population into two numerically equal halves.

title: Highest Foreign-Born Population Share
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of foreign-born residents (immigrants as % of population).

source.name: UN DESA — International Migrant Stock

note: Gulf states dominate due to migrant labor systems. Vatican City is technically ~100% foreign-born but not always reported. Excludes territories and dependencies.

title: Most Bordering Countries
prompt: Name the countries that border the most other sovereign countries.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Land Boundaries

note: Russia and China tie at 14 land neighbors each. This ranking counts only sovereign UN member states; disputed territories like Kosovo/Palestine are excluded by some sources, which changes counts.

title: Lowest Population (Smallest Countries)
prompt: Name the sovereign UN member (or observer) states with the smallest population.

source.name: UN World Population Prospects 2024

note: Vatican City is a UN observer state, not a member. Excludes dependent territories (Pitcairn Islands, Tokelau, etc.). Tuvalu and Nauru regularly swap positions.

title: Highest Average Elevation
prompt: Name the countries with the highest mean elevation above sea level.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Elevation extremes / mean elevation

note: Bhutan is sometimes included with a higher mean elevation but the CIA WFB does not publish a mean figure for it. Bolivia's high figure reflects the Altiplano dominating its populated west, though Amazon lowlands cover its east.

title: Highest Life Expectancy at Birth
prompt: Which countries have the highest life expectancy at birth?

source.name: UN World Population Prospects 2024

note: Microstates (Monaco, San Marino) are excluded per UN WPP methodology; this is the standard sovereign-state ranking.

title: Most Physicians per 1,000 People
prompt: Which countries have the most physicians per 1,000 people?

source.name: World Bank / WHO Global Health Workforce Statistics

note: Cuba's high figure reflects broad training programs; Monaco and San Marino excluded as microstates skew the top ranks.

title: Highest Health Expenditure as % of GDP
prompt: Which countries spend the most on healthcare as a share of GDP?

source.name: World Bank / WHO Global Health Expenditure Database

note: Includes public and private spending; the US leads by a wide margin among large economies.

title: Highest Obesity Rate (Adults)
prompt: Which countries have the highest adult obesity rates?

source.name: WHO Global Health Observatory (BMI ≥ 30)

note: Pacific Island nations dominate the top ranks; the game shows sovereign states only. Values reflect WHO age-standardized estimates for adults 18+.

title: Highest Suicide Rate
prompt: Which countries have the highest suicide rates per 100,000 people?

source.name: WHO Global Health Estimates

note: Age-standardized rate per 100,000 people, both sexes. Reporting quality varies significantly across countries.

title: Highest Cancer Incidence Rate
prompt: Which countries have the highest age-standardized cancer incidence rates?

source.name: IARC Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN)

note: High rates in wealthy nations reflect longer lifespans and better cancer detection/registries, not necessarily worse cancer causation.

title: Lowest Infant Mortality Rate
prompt: Which countries have the lowest infant mortality rate (deaths under 1 year per 1,000 live births)?

source.name: UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation (UN IGME)

note: Reporting definitions vary; some countries do not count extremely premature births as live births, which can artificially lower rates.

title: Most Hospital Beds per 1,000 People
prompt: Which countries have the most hospital beds per 1,000 people?

source.name: World Bank / OECD Health Statistics

note: Includes all inpatient beds. North Korea's high figure reflects self-reported data; hospital bed density does not always correlate with care quality.

title: Largest active military personnel
prompt: Name the countries with the most active-duty military personnel.

source.name: IISS — The Military Balance 2024
source.asOf: IISS Military Balance 2024 (data as of late 2023)

note: Active-duty uniformed personnel only. Excludes reserves and paramilitaries. North Korea's figure is IISS's central estimate; open-source estimates vary.

title: Largest defense budget
prompt: Name the countries with the highest military expenditure (in US dollars).

source.name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database

note: Current US-dollar figures for 2024. China, Russia, Saudi Arabia and Israel figures are SIPRI estimates. Ukraine excludes external military aid.

title: Countries with nuclear weapons (warhead stockpiles)
prompt: Name the nine states known or believed to possess nuclear weapons, ranked by estimated total inventory.

source.name: SIPRI Yearbook 2024 / Federation of American Scientists

note: Total inventory including deployed, stored, and retired-but-intact warheads. Israel neither confirms nor denies its arsenal. North Korea's count is highly uncertain — SIPRI estimates ~50 assembled warheads but material for more.

title: Highest military spending as share of GDP
prompt: Name the countries that spend the highest share of their GDP on the military.

source.name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database

note: Percentage of GDP spent on the military in 2024. Ukraine's share reflects wartime mobilization. Excludes countries where SIPRI cannot produce a reliable estimate.

title: Largest arms exporters
prompt: Name the countries with the biggest share of major-conventional-weapons exports over the past five years.

source.name: SIPRI Arms Transfers Database (Trend Indicator Value)

note: Global share of major-conventional-weapons exports measured by SIPRI's Trend Indicator Value (TIV) — a volume metric, not a dollar figure. Covers 2019–2023 combined.

title: Largest arms importers
prompt: Name the countries with the biggest share of major-conventional-weapons imports over the past five years.

source.name: SIPRI Arms Transfers Database (Trend Indicator Value)

note: Global share of major-conventional-weapons imports measured by SIPRI's Trend Indicator Value (TIV). Ukraine's rise reflects deliveries from allies since Russia's 2022 invasion.

title: Most main battle tanks in active service
prompt: Name the countries with the most main battle tanks in active service.

source.name: IISS — The Military Balance 2024
source.asOf: IISS Military Balance 2024 (data as of late 2023)

note: Active-inventory main battle tanks (MBTs) only, excluding stored/reserve fleets. Russia's active fleet has been sharply reduced by losses in Ukraine; totals including storage would rank Russia far higher.

title: Highest World Happiness Report Score
prompt: Which countries have the highest happiness scores according to the World Happiness Report?

source.name: World Happiness Report 2024 (Gallup / UN SDSN / Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre)

note: Score is a 0-10 life-evaluation ladder average from Gallup World Poll respondents.

title: Least Corrupt Countries (Corruption Perceptions Index)
prompt: According to Transparency International, which countries are perceived as least corrupt in the public sector?

source.name: Transparency International Corruption Perceptions Index 2023

note: Higher score (out of 100) = less perceived corruption. Ties share the same rank.

title: Highest Human Development Index
prompt: Which countries rank highest on the UNDP Human Development Index?

source.name: UNDP Human Development Report 2023/2024

note: HDI is a composite of life expectancy, education, and GNI per capita. Scored 0-1.

title: Most Peaceful Countries (Global Peace Index)
prompt: According to the Institute for Economics & Peace, which countries are the most peaceful?

source.name: Global Peace Index 2024 (Institute for Economics & Peace)

note: Lower score = more peaceful. Composite of 23 indicators covering conflict, safety, and militarization.

title: Highest Press Freedom (Reporters Without Borders)
prompt: According to Reporters Without Borders, which countries have the most press freedom?

source.name: RSF World Press Freedom Index 2024

note: Higher score (out of 100) = more press freedom.

title: Smallest Gender Gap (WEF Global Gender Gap Index)
prompt: According to the World Economic Forum, which countries have closed the largest share of their gender gap?

source.name: World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Report 2024

note: Score is the share of the gender gap closed (0 = imparity, 1 = parity) across economic, education, health, and political dimensions.

title: Highest Incarceration Rate per Capita
prompt: Which countries have the highest prison population rate per 100,000 people?

source.name: World Prison Brief (Institute for Crime & Justice Policy Research)

note: Rate is prison population per 100,000 of the national population.

title: Most Refugees Hosted
prompt: Which countries host the largest refugee populations?

source.name: UNHCR Global Trends: Forced Displacement in 2023

note: Includes refugees under UNHCR's mandate plus Palestine refugees under UNRWA's mandate where applicable. Absolute counts, not per capita.

title: Most FIFA Men's World Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most FIFA Men's World Cup titles.

source.name: FIFA — Men's World Cup History

note: Only 8 nations have ever won. West Germany's titles (1954, 1974, 1990) are credited to Germany per FIFA.

title: Most FIFA Women's World Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most FIFA Women's World Cup titles.

source.name: FIFA — Women's World Cup History
source.asOf: After 2023 World Cup (Australia/New Zealand); next edition 2027

note: Only 5 nations have ever won since the tournament began in 1991.

title: Most Summer Olympic gold medals (all-time)
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time Summer Olympic gold medals.

source.name: International Olympic Committee — All-time Summer Olympic medal table

note: Soviet Union medals (1952–1988) are counted separately from Russia and are excluded here to avoid the Soviet/Unified Team/Russia confusion. Germany combines West/East/unified totals per IOC convention.

title: Most Winter Olympic gold medals (all-time)
prompt: Name the countries with the most all-time Winter Olympic gold medals.

source.name: International Olympic Committee — All-time Winter Olympic medal table

note: Soviet Union (78 gold, 1956–1988) is listed separately by the IOC and excluded here to avoid mixing with modern Russia.

title: Most Rugby (Union) World Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most Rugby World Cup titles.

source.name: World Rugby — Rugby World Cup History
source.asOf: After 2023 Rugby World Cup (France); next edition 2027

note: Only 4 nations have ever won the men's Rugby World Cup since its 1987 inception.

title: Most ICC Men's Cricket World Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries with the most ICC Men's Cricket World Cup (ODI) titles.

source.name: International Cricket Council — Men's Cricket World Cup History
source.asOf: After 2023 Cricket World Cup (India); next edition 2027

note: 50-over ODI World Cup only. Does not include T20 World Cup or Champions Trophy.

title: Most Formula 1 Constructors' Championships
prompt: Name the countries with the most F1 Constructors' Championships (by team headquarters/nationality).

source.name: Formula 1 — Official F1 Records

note: Nationality assigned by the team's constructor license country (e.g. Ferrari = Italy, McLaren/Williams/Mercedes = UK, Red Bull = Austria). Constructors' Championship began in 1958.

title: Highest FIFA Men's World Ranking (Elo-based)
prompt: Name the top-ranked men's national football teams in the current FIFA World Ranking.

source.name: FIFA/Coca-Cola Men's World Ranking

note: FIFA uses an Elo-based points system. Rankings shift frequently; these reflect the April 2025 publication.

title: Fastest fixed broadband internet speed
prompt: Name the countries with the fastest median fixed broadband download speeds.

source.name: Ookla Speedtest Global Index

note: Ookla only publishes a rolling monthly snapshot and blocks archive.org, so historical data is not retrievable. Median download speed in Mbps. Small territories (Hong Kong, Macau) are ranked separately by Ookla.

title: Fastest mobile internet speed
prompt: Name the countries with the fastest median mobile internet download speeds.

source.name: Ookla Speedtest Global Index

note: Median mobile download speed in Mbps. Gulf states dominate due to aggressive 5G rollout. Kosovo uses ISO user-assigned code XK (not officially in ISO 3166-1).

title: Most internet users (total)
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total number of internet users.

source.name: ITU / DataReportal Digital 2024
source.asOf: India from DataReportal Jan 2024; other countries ITU 2021 (latest complete cross-country dataset)

note: India's ITU 2021 figure (608M) was updated to the DataReportal Digital 2024 figure (~752M) since India's user base has grown rapidly. Absolute rank ordering has been stable since 2021.

title: Highest internet penetration
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population using the internet.

source.name: ITU (via Wikipedia list of countries by Internet users)

note: Microstates under 500K population (Monaco, Liechtenstein, San Marino, etc.) were excluded to keep answers recognizable. ITU rounds up to 100% for several Gulf states, causing a 4-way tie at #1.

title: Most patents granted (by origin)
prompt: Name the countries whose residents were granted the most patents in a year.

source.name: WIPO World Intellectual Property Indicators 2024

note: Metric is patent grants by origin (applicant's country of residence), which counts a country's inventors regardless of which patent office granted the patent. Different from grants-by-office, which would put China even higher.

title: Most scientific research papers published
prompt: Name the countries that published the most scientific research documents in a year.

source.name: SCImago Journal & Country Rank (Scopus data)

note: Counts documents indexed by Scopus (journal articles, conference papers, reviews). China overtook the US around 2018 and has continued to widen the gap.

title: Highest R&D expenditure (% of GDP)
prompt: Name the countries that spend the largest share of GDP on research and development.

source.name: World Bank (indicator GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS)

note: Also called GERD (Gross domestic Expenditure on R&D). Israel and South Korea consistently top the list. Singapore's value is 2020 (its most recent). Denmark and Iceland are tied at #12.

title: Most supercomputers in the TOP500
prompt: Name the countries with the most systems on the TOP500 supercomputer list.

source.name: TOP500 List

note: The TOP500 project ranks the world's most powerful non-distributed computer systems twice a year. Systems are counted by the country hosting the machine, not manufacturer. Multiple ties in the lower half of the top 20.
